headline: Earnings and premium volume pull back as buybacks accelerate
summary_short: Net income fell 17.8% y/y to $559M ($14.22 diluted EPS) as the Group combined ratio rose to 92.0% from 90.4% y/y on higher catastrophe losses and softer reinsurance pricing; the company repurchased $395M of shares in the quarter.
summary_long: Revenue fell 11.8% y/y to $3.96B and net income fell 17.8% y/y to $559M as Reinsurance Treaty gross premium declined 9.1% (comparable basis) on softer Casualty pricing and pre-tax catastrophe losses rose to $94M from $20M y/y, driven mainly by Iran War and mid-sized event losses. Net investment income slipped to $523M from $532M on lower alternative-investment returns. Cash fell to $1.12B from $1.90B y/y after $725M of YTD buybacks; shareholders' equity rose 2.7% y/y to $15.43B and book value per share rose to $398.83 from $358.08 y/y. Weighted diluted shares fell 7.2% y/y on Q2's $395M of repurchases. No numeric forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: Group combined ratio rose to 92.0% from 90.4% y/y on higher catastrophe losses (Iran War and mid-sized events) and softer reinsurance treaty pricing, partly offset by continued share buybacks.
Reinsurance Treaty gross premium fell 9.1% (comparable basis) led by declines in Casualty XOL (-25.0%) and Casualty Pro-Rata (-22.8%), partly offset by Property Pro-Rata growth (+3.4%).
Net investment income dipped to $523M from $532M on lower alternative-investment returns, while pre-tax catastrophe losses rose to $94M from $20M y/y, mainly Iran War and mid-sized events.
Cash fell as $725M of YTD share repurchases and investment portfolio reallocation (net purchases of fixed maturities) outpaced operating cash inflows.
